pages.title: Liquid Metallic Hydrogen
pages.text: Hydrogen compressed until it becomes a metal. At pressures found in the cores of gas giants, the electrons break free and conduct like copper. It flows silvery and heavy, and may be a room-temperature superconductor.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Wigner and Huntington predicted metallic hydrogen in 1935. Crushing degenerate matter with superfluid helium in the Neutron Star Forge, I found hydrogen that conducted like a metal.
